plan.title: Confounded lung treated vs control DE analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The design has 6 treated and 6 control lung samples, but batch B2 holds all treated samples and B1 holds all controls — batch is perfectly confounded with condition. This means any 'condition effect' found is statistically inseparable from a batch/processing effect: the model matrix cannot carry both terms, and no correction method (ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, SVA) can remove batch without also removing the biological signal. The plan follows the grounded procedure: (1) QC via blind VST + PCA + sample-distance heatmap to show whether samples separate along condition/batch (they are identical axes here), (2) minimal count pre-filter, (3) DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization, (4) a ~condition-only model (no batch term — not identifiable) with the confound stated explicitly as an assumption, (5) Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, (6) BH FDR at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, (7) an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test run in parallel on the same design as a second-method robustness check per R-0001/R-0042, reporting the overlap as the higher-confidence set, (8) over-representation enrichment (not preranked GSEA, which the knowledge check rejected for this situation) against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets using the tested-gene universe, and (9) a report that states plainly every result is confounded with batch and cannot be attributed to treatment alone — the underlying biological question this dataset was collected to answer cannot be safely answered from these samples.
